readme.html:
Use your Claude subscription to run pentests. No API key needed.

ARTEX is an autonomous penetration testing platform that exposes upstream ARTEX's pentest model as MCP tools Claude Code calls through your existing Claude subscription. Asset graph, exploration tracking, finding management, coverage recording, traffic capture, and report generation, exposed as 65 MCP tools. No separate LLM API key, no token budget, no agent loop of its own.

You bring the brain. ARTEX brings the hands.

Documentation · Live demo · Getting started

Authorized use only. This is an offensive security tool, for penetration testing, red teaming, CTFs and lab work. Use it only against systems you own or have explicit permission to test.

How it works

Claude Code decides what to test, what tools to call, and in what order. ARTEX executes the calls: inserting assets, tracking the exploration graph, recording findings and credentials, logging coverage, and capturing HTTP traffic through its built-in recording proxy. The exploration graph keeps Claude oriented across long engagements, so a session you stop today resumes tomorrow with graph_overview.

$ claude
> Pentest example.com, starting with reconnaissance.

Claude calls: graph_overview → set_goals → insert_assets (domain: example.com)
         → add_intent (enumerate subdomains) → record_fact (found: api.example.com)
         → insert_assets (subdomain: api.example.com, service: https/443)
         → add_intent (test api.example.com for auth bypass)
         → traffic_hosts → traffic_search (host: api.example.com)
         → traffic_get (inspect the auth request)
         → traffic_replay (replay with modified auth header)
         → record_coverage (api /admin, idor, no_issue_found)
         → report_finding (severity: high, broken access control on /api/v2/users)
         → prove_goal (evidence: finding #1) → generate_report

Eval: HTB Forest (blind, no writeups)

ARTEX + Claude Opus 5.5 against Forest, a classic Active Directory box, with no web searches, writeups or hints. AS-REP roast to a foothold, then Exchange Windows Permissions to DCSync and Domain Admin. Both flags in ~8 minutes, with cleanup afterwards. Full walkthrough: artex-cc.com/evals/htb-forest.

Web UI

artex-cc serve --web adds a dashboard on the same port as the MCP endpoint: the exploration graph, findings with their bound traffic, coverage, credentials, and a printable report, updated live. See Web UI.

Install

brew install --cask sresarehumantoo/tap/artex-cc

Docker Compose, pre-built binaries and go install are covered in Getting started.

Quick start

With PostgreSQL running:

createdb ccartex
artex-cc init --pg "postgres://localhost/ccartex" --goal "Pentest example.com"

Add the server to Claude Code (~/.claude.json or a project .mcp.json):

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "artex": {
      "command": "artex-cc",
      "args": ["serve", "--stdio", "--pg", "postgres://localhost/ccartex", "--proxy", ":8788"]
    }
  }
}

Start Claude Code and ask it to "pentest example.com, starting with reconnaissance". For Docker, other MCP clients and proxy CA trust, see Getting started.
